Definition: a berry (as if a pellet of rumination)
BiblicalUsage: Gargar is a berry, the few olives left after the shaking. Yet gleaning grapes shall be left in it, says Isaiah 17:6, as the shaking of an olive tree — two or three berries in the top of the uppermost bough, four or five in the outmost fruitful branches. The word is the small remnant after the harvest.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the two or three berries are the remnant God always keeps; the tree is shaken and the harvest is taken, yet a few remain in the topmost bough; I hold that God never leaves Himself without a remnant.
